key_insight: A longitudinal machine learning model using routine EHR data could flag people at high risk for incident inflammatory bowel disease months to years before diagnosis.
clinical_relevance: If prospectively validated, this approach could help clinicians find patients with undiagnosed IBD earlier and potentially shorten diagnostic delay.
method: Trained a Mamba state-space model on pre-diagnostic EHR data from adults with IBD-compatible symptoms/signs/finding.
Excluded diagnostic-workup features to focus on pre-workup signals of future IBD.
Externally validated the model at a demographically distinct safety-net hospital and simulated a diagnosis-code-only alert workflow.
evidence_signal: At 6 months after presentation, Mamba achieved AUROC 0.969 at UCSF and 0.965 at ZSFG, with median lead times of 20 and 15 months, respectively.
watch_item: This was a retrospective study, so real-world alert performance, false positives, and impact on outcomes still need prospective evaluation.
paper_title: Prediction of incident inflammatory bowel disease from routine electronic health records: development and external validation of a longitudinal machine learning model
